Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

robbery noun

also robberies, armed robbery, highway robbery, hold-up

classical

Cic. Cat. 2.1: in apertum latrōcinium (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 191, 196

latrōcinium, latrōciniī n.

noun, second declension

robbery, brigandage

Other words

  • rapīna, rapīnae f. — robbery, plunder

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Cat. 2.10: nisi caedēs, nisi incendia, nisi rapīnās (Lewis & Short)

    In prose before Augustus, and in Tacitus and Suetonius, only in the plural (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • Latrōcinium modo factum est.

    A robbery has just taken place.Traupman 191

  • Arguentur dē vī et manū atque latrōciniō.

    They will be charged with assault and battery as well as robbery.Traupman 191

See also rob, theft, thief, burglar.

SourcesLewis & Short: latrocinium · Lewis & Short: rapina

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 191, 196.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
